privacy_meta_description: Braggster keeps your scores on your device. No accounts, no ads, no cookies. We collect crash diagnostics and anonymous usage counts, which you can switch off, and anonymous counts if you play online.
privacy_intro: Braggster keeps your scores on your phone. There are no accounts and no server that stores your games. The only server we run is a relay for online Live Tables, which cannot read the games it passes on and also receives the anonymous usage counts. We collect three things: crash diagnostics and anonymous usage statistics, which you can both switch off in Settings, and anonymous counts from online tables. Here is what that means in practice.
privacy_collect_p: Three things. First, crash diagnostics. When the app crashes, Firebase Crashlytics sends us the crash details, your device model, your OS version and an install id that Crashlytics generates itself. It is not linked to your identity and is never used to track you. It is on by default, and you can turn it off under Send crash reports in Settings, which also deletes any reports still waiting to be sent. Second, if you play an online Live Table, anonymous counts from the relay, described under Online Live Tables below. Third, anonymous usage statistics: which games and puzzles are played each day, described under Anonymous usage statistics below. Nothing else is collected: no advertising, no trackers, and no analytics beyond those anonymous usage and relay counts. We never see your games, your players, or your scores.
privacy_stored_p: Your games, players, scores and settings are stored only on your device. If you delete the app, that data is gone. If you share a game with another device, it travels straight between the two devices and never passes through us.
privacy_online_p1: When you play a Live Table online, the phones at the table connect through a relay server that we run on Microsoft Azure in West Europe, inside the EU. To connect the players, the relay processes your IP address while you are connected, and it never stores it. What happens in the game is end-to-end encrypted between the phones, so the relay passes it on without being able to read it, and neither can we.
privacy_online_p2: The relay keeps anonymous statistics: how many matches and rooms there were, which game was played at a table, how long messages take to arrive in milliseconds, and which app versions connected. It also notes which country players connect from. When you connect, the relay works out the country from your IP address and keeps only the two-letter country code, never the address. Countries are only ever shown as 30-day totals, and a country with fewer than 5 matches is grouped as Other. None of this contains identifiers or anything that identifies a player, it is not linked to you, and it is never used to track you. We delete it after 31 days.
privacy_online_p3: Playing on the same Wi-Fi is unaffected. A table that stays on Wi-Fi does not use the relay at all.
privacy_usage_p1: On your phone, the app counts which games and puzzles are played each day: the game, how it was played (keeping score on a scorecard, playing in the app on one phone, a Live Table, or a puzzle) and, for a puzzle, its difficulty. That is all. The counts carry no identifier of any kind: no install id, no device id, no account, no player names, no scores, no app version and no location. Once a day the app sends the finished days, at most the last 7, to our own server, the same relay on Microsoft Azure in West Europe, inside the EU. The server keeps only the counts. It uses your IP address only in memory, to limit how often reports can be sent, and never stores it, and it does not work out a country for these reports. We delete the statistics after 31 days.
privacy_usage_p2: Usage statistics are on by default. You can turn them off under Share anonymous usage statistics in Settings, which also deletes any counts not yet sent. They are not linked to you and are never used to track you.
privacy_share_p: We sell nothing to anyone. Crash diagnostics go to Firebase Crashlytics, a Google service, and we use them only to fix bugs. Online Live Tables and the anonymous usage counts go through our own relay, hosted by Microsoft Azure in the EU, which handles the traffic for us as described above. We do not share the usage counts with anyone. If you buy a game, Apple or Google handles the payment; we never see your card details and we have no server that records what you bought. Apart from what is described above and the games you choose to share with other players, nothing leaves your device, so there is nothing else to share.
privacy_website_p: braggster.com is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages. It uses Microsoft Clarity to see which parts of the page people read and where they get stuck. Clarity runs in cookieless mode here: it sets no cookies, it cannot recognise you across visits, and it gets a fresh anonymous id on every page view. It receives your IP address, your browser, your device type, and the clicks and scrolling you do on the page. We use this only to improve the site, and we never combine it with anything from the app. GitHub also keeps standard server logs, including your IP address, to serve the page and guard against abuse.
privacy_children_p: Braggster is suitable for all ages. The crash diagnostics, the anonymous usage statistics and the anonymous relay counts above are the only things we collect from anyone, child or adult. They are not linked to identity, never used for tracking, and you can switch the crash diagnostics and the usage statistics off in Settings.
privacy_rights_p: Under the GDPR you can access, correct and delete your personal data. We hold nothing that identifies you: crash diagnostics, usage counts and relay counts are not linked to your identity, so we cannot tie them back to you, the relay does not store IP addresses, and your games, players and scores stay on your device or travel end-to-end encrypted, so we cannot read them. If you would rather send nothing at all, turn off crash reports and the anonymous usage statistics in Settings, and play on the same Wi-Fi instead of online.
privacy_changes_p: If this policy changes, we will update this page and the date above.
privacy_contact_p: Questions about privacy? Mail us at
support_meta_description: Need a hand with Braggster? Email support@braggster.com and we will help you get back to game night.
support_intro: Something not working, or just have a question? We are glad to help. Braggster keeps everything on your device, so there is no account to recover: nearly everything can be sorted out over email.
support_email_p: The fastest way to reach us is email. Write to us at
support_include_p: To help us help you quickly, tell us your device and its OS version, the game you were scoring, and what you expected to happen against what actually did. A screenshot goes a long way.
support_response_p: We are a small team and we read every message. You can expect a reply within a few working days.

terms_meta_description: The terms for using Braggster, a local-first score keeper. Covers the free trial, one-time unlocks, the yearly subscription and its auto-renewal, and fair use.
terms_intro: These terms are the agreement between you and Braggster for using the app and this website. By downloading or using Braggster you accept them. If you do not agree, please do not use the app.
terms_app_p: Braggster keeps score for card, board, dice, puzzle and sports games. We grant you a personal, non-transferable licence to use it on your own devices. You may not resell it, rent it out, or try to copy, decompile or reverse engineer it beyond what the law allows.
terms_trial_p: Every game is free to try for your first 10 plays across the whole app. The Blank scorecard and the Freestyle table stay free forever, and you also keep one premium game of your choice for free. After the trial you can keep playing the rest with a one-time unlock or a subscription.
terms_purchases_p: Braggster offers a one-time lifetime unlock and an auto-renewing yearly subscription. The price is shown before you buy. The yearly subscription renews automatically at the same price each year unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the current period ends. You can view, manage or cancel it any time in your Apple or Google account settings; cancelling stops the next renewal and keeps your access until the period ends. All payments, renewals and refunds are handled by Apple or Google under their terms, not by us.
terms_conduct_p: Please use Braggster only for keeping score of the games you play. Do not use it unlawfully, or try to break, overload or interfere with the app or this website.
terms_nowager_p: Braggster records points, not money. No game stakes or pays out a bet, chip, pot or ante, and the app is for entertainment only. It is not a gambling product and offers no real or simulated gambling.
terms_ip_p: Braggster and its logo are ours. Game names are used only to say which game a scorecard is for; all trademarks belong to their respective owners, and Braggster is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by any of them. Every brand name can be switched to a plain generic description in Settings.
terms_warranty_p: Braggster is provided as is, without warranties of any kind. We do our best to keep it working and accurate, but we cannot guarantee it will be uninterrupted or error free.
terms_liability_p: To the extent the law allows, Braggster is not liable for any indirect or incidental loss arising from your use of the app or this website. Nothing in these terms limits rights you have that cannot be waived under the law that applies to you.
terms_law_p: These terms are governed by the law of the Netherlands, without affecting any mandatory consumer protections of the country where you live.
terms_changes_p: If these terms change, we will update this page and the date above. Continuing to use Braggster after a change means you accept the updated terms.

home_faq_q1: Can we play on several phones at once?
home_faq_a1: Yes. With Play together, one phone starts a table and shows a code, and the others scan it or pick the table from a list. Each player then plays from their own phone. It works for Yahtzee, Chess, Checkers, International draughts, Backgammon and Othello.
home_faq_q2: Do I need internet or an account?
home_faq_a2: No. Braggster has no accounts and works offline. Play together only needs the phones to be on the same Wi-Fi: nothing goes over the internet or through a server, and the connection between the phones is encrypted.
home_faq_q3: Can iPhone and Android play together?
home_faq_a3: Yes. iPhones and Android phones can sit at the same table. Only the host needs the game, so joining is free, even if you do not own it.
home_faq_q4: Which games can I play against the computer?
home_faq_a4: Six games: Chess, Checkers, International draughts, Backgammon, Othello and Hearts, each at three levels: Easy, Medium and Hard. Practice games do not count toward your statistics.
home_faq_a5: The download is free and every game is free for your first 10 plays. The Blank scorecard, the Freestyle table and one game of your choice stay free forever. After that you can unlock every game once, or take a yearly subscription. There are no ads.
home_faq_a6: Seven: English, Dutch, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese (Brazil) and Italian.

pt_meta_title: Play together on several phones: braggster
pt_meta_description: Play Yahtzee, Chess, Backgammon and more with a phone each over the same Wi-Fi. Scan a code to join. No account, no internet, iPhone and Android together.
pt_intro: Play together puts one live match on every phone at the table. One player starts it, the others scan a code, and everyone plays from their own phone over the same Wi-Fi. No account, no internet and no server.
pt_how_h2: At the table in three steps
pt_step1_body: Open a game that supports Play together and tap Start a table. Your phone shows a QR code, and you are the host.
pt_step2_body: Everyone else opens braggster on their own phone, on the same Wi-Fi, and taps Scan a code. The table also shows up under Tables on this Wi-Fi, so they can pick it from the list instead.
pt_step3_body: A scanned code lets a player straight in; someone who picked the table from the list waits for you to tap Accept. Then you start the match, and everyone plays their own seat on their own phone.
pt_games_intro: Each of these also works on a single phone. With Play together, every player takes a seat on their own phone instead.
pt_dice_body: The host switches on digital dice for the table. When it is your turn you throw on your own phone, and everyone else watches the dice land on theirs. Up to six players, a phone each.
pt_marks_body: On the boards, the last move is marked on both phones, so you can see what your opponent just did the moment you look down.
pt_privacy_body: The phones talk to each other directly over your local network. There is no braggster server in between, nothing goes over the internet, and the connection between each phone and the host is encrypted.
pt_free_body: Only the host needs the game. Anyone who joins can play without buying it or using up a free play, so one phone never holds up the table. The match counts in every player's own statistics.
pt_faq_q1: Do we need an internet connection?
pt_faq_a1: No. The phones only need to be on the same Wi-Fi. Nothing goes over the internet, and there is no account to create.
pt_faq_a2: No. Play together runs over Wi-Fi, which is what lets iPhones and Android phones join the same table.
pt_faq_q3: Can iPhone and Android players join the same table?
pt_faq_a3: Yes. A table can mix iPhones and Android phones freely.
pt_faq_a4: Chess, Checkers, International draughts, Backgammon and Othello are two-player games, so two phones. Yahtzee takes up to six players, a phone each.
pt_faq_q5: Does a Play together match count in my statistics?
pt_faq_a5: Yes. The match is saved on every phone at the table and counts in each player's own statistics. Practice games against the computer do not.
pt_faq_q6: Why can't my friend find the table?
pt_faq_a6: Check that both phones are on the same Wi-Fi, and on an iPhone allow braggster to use the local network. If the table still does not show up in the list, scan the host's code instead.
